findings.evidence: Both address worship of entities other than Allah; 21:66 challenges their inability to benefit or harm.
37:162 says idolaters cannot lead astray except those destined for punishment; 15:42 denies Satan authority over God's servants except followers.
37:163 describes those destined for Hell, 15:43 Hell as the appointed destination.
Angels speaking of their assigned station; 19:64 angels descend only by God's command.
الصافون / الصافات shared root and ranks; interpretive angel context to verify in tafsir.
Angelic ranks and standing in rows; requires target Arabic verification.
Angels glorifying Allah; 21:20 explicitly describes continual glorification.
Victory promised to messengers in both verses.
37:179 warns opponents they will see; 15:87 grants the seven oft-repeated verses and the great Qur'an; no direct semantic parallel identified.
37:180 exalts Lord of might above their descriptions; 15:87 concerns revelation of seven oft-repeated verses; no close thematic or narrative connection.
Both exalt Lord of the Throne above improper descriptions, while 21:22 adds monotheistic argument.
